LESSON: MANAGING WASTE ENVIRONMENT

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Care for the
Topic 3.3: Managing waste environment

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Managing waste environment. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MANAGING WASTE ENVIRONMENT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Managing waste environment helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: MANAGING WASTE ENVIRONMENT
Study Managing waste environment like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Managing waste environment” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Managing waste environment is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Managing waste environment” around your school. (skill: appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Managing waste environment to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Managing waste environment from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Managing waste environment: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Managing waste environment?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Managing waste environment means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate a clean classroom environment for good health.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
